explanation: Conditional compilation in C is a preprocessor directive that allows specific parts of the code to be included or excluded during compilation based on whether certain macros are defined. It is used to create portable and flexible code that can adapt to different environments, such as various operating systems, without changing the source code.
code_example: #define MY_OS  // Defines a macro for demonstration
example_explanation: This example defines a macro named MY_OS and uses the #ifdef directive to check if it is defined. If defined, it prints 'The macro is defined', demonstrating how conditional compilation includes the printf statement only when the macro exists, thus showing the core mechanism in a simple, runnable program.

extraction_metadata.source: The C Programming Language - Kernighan & Ritchie
